fact: La Poste Tunisienne provides free e-Dinar wallets and the D17 app for remote payments, used by about 1,568,000 pupils for 2026-27 school registration (La Presse de Tunisie).
The Fintech Times says Flouci offers an app combining electronic payments and financial services, and Konnect and Paymee accept La Poste's e-Dinar products.
The Central Bank of Tunisia's Bulletin No. 15 reports mobile payments of 8.4 million transactions worth 1.769 billion dinars in 2025, up 81% in transactions.
Banks, payment institutions and the postal service operate electronic wallet services, and BCT data show 8.4 million mobile transactions worth 1.769 billion dinars in 2025.
The BCT note says Societe Monetique Tunisie manages the mobile payment system in Tunisia, and banks, the Post and payment institutions issue mobile wallets.
La Presse says OFT Tunisie, licensed as a payment institution, must begin operating within six months and will offer payment accounts, local person-to-person transfers, bill and online payments.
African Manager says Tunisian payment institutions operate payment accounts at three levels, with balance caps of TND 500, 1,000 and 5,000 under Circular 2018-16, to be raised under Circular 2026-10.

The Banque Centrale de Tunisie bulletin on 2024 reports mobile payment activity through payment service provider wallets (368,595 in the 2024 column), with payments, transfers, cash-in and cash-out transactions.
